name: CD-ROM
purpose: holds about an album's worth of data on a disc that is pressed once and never changed
looks_like: a shiny disc twelve centimetres across, silver underneath, with a hole in the middle
note: The RO means read-only, and it is the whole reason a bought CD cannot be recorded over. The word „CD" alone hides that — a CD-R and a CD-RW are different things wearing almost the same name

name: DVD
purpose: holds a film, or a few gigabytes of files, on a disc the same size as a CD
looks_like: the same shiny twelve-centimetre disc as a CD — you cannot tell them apart by eye, only by the label
note: The V once stood for Video and was changed to Versatile when it turned out people wanted to put anything on it. Seven times a CD, in the same shape

name: Blu-ray
purpose: holds a film in high resolution, on a disc read by a blue laser instead of a red one
looks_like: again the same twelve-centimetre disc, usually in a blue case rather than a black one
note: Named after the laser, not the case: a shorter wavelength reads smaller pits, which is the entire trick behind five times a DVD in the same space

name: Hard disk
purpose: holds everything on a computer on spinning magnetic platters, cheaply and in quantity
looks_like: a sealed metal box about the size of a pack of cards, heavy for its size, and it makes a faint noise while it works
note: The only medium here with moving parts, which is why it is the only one that can be killed by being dropped while it runs — and why it is the one that warns you with a noise first

name: SSD
purpose: does a hard disk's job with no moving parts, so it answers far faster and makes no sound
looks_like: a flat plastic box, or a stick the size of a chewing-gum strip plugged flat onto the board
note: „Solid state" means nothing moves — the word is about the absence of mechanics, not about sturdiness, although it delivers that too. The single biggest reason an old computer feels new after one is fitted

name: SD card
purpose: holds the pictures a camera takes, on a card small enough to forget in a pocket
looks_like: a flat plastic card about the size of a postage stamp, with one corner cut off at an angle
note: The cut corner is not decoration: it is what stops the card going in the wrong way round. There is a smaller one too — microSD — and the adapter that makes it the bigger one is just a plastic frame

name: USB stick
purpose: holds files on something you carry in a pocket and plug into any computer
looks_like: a thumb-sized plastic or metal body with a USB plug at one end, often with a cap that gets lost
note: Inside it is the same kind of memory as an SSD and an SD card — three things that look nothing alike and differ mainly in the plug they wear

name: Floppy disk
purpose: held a document or two on a magnetic disc in a plastic sleeve — the way files moved between computers before networks
looks_like: a square plastic case about nine centimetres across with a sliding metal shutter
note: Still the Save icon in almost every program, thirty years after the last person used one. A whole generation recognises the picture and has never seen the object
